content:
lina: Quick question for the group — prepping an on‑prem customer rollout that wants packet mirroring to our IDS collector. Need advice on netpols + KMS/audit implications.
carla: TL;DR — mirroring is fine but treat mirrored stream as sensitive by default. Masking/filtering before egress if possible.
sam: +1. Also check bounce paths: mirrored traffic often goes out of the tenant VPC to a collector subnet. Who manages that collector in this deployment?
lina: Collector is customer-managed but we host the analysis cluster in a dedicated subnet inside their VPC. We requested a private peering to our ops subnet.
igor: Two immediate concerns: 1) mirrored payload could capture auth headers or tokens, 2) audit trails for who requested mirroring and key usage must exist.
carla: For (1) enforce netpol egress deny-by-default and explicit allow to collector IPs only. At the netpol level, drop hostNetwork pods from mirroring, and exclude nginx ingress debug headers.
ops: If you want a snippet, this is what we deploy as a default egress netpol to limit mirror exporter pods:
```yaml
kind: NetworkPolicy
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
metadata:
  name: mirror-exporter-egress
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: mirror-exporter
  policyTypes:
    - Egress
  egress:
    - to:
      - ipBlock:
          cidr: 10.200.5.0/24
      ports:
        - protocol: TCP
          port: 9200
```
sam: Keep the IP range small and pinned. Also ensure the exporter runs with a read-only serviceaccount that can't access secrets.
lina: KMS question: will mirrored traffic potentially leak plaintext if we mirror decrypted layers from the runtime? The runtime decrypts tokens with KMS locally before sending outbound calls.
igor: Yes — if the mirror taps the process boundary (e.g., userspace) you can capture plaintext. Options: mirror only network-level (L2/L3) or ensure runtime never emits secrets on the wire in plaintext.
carla: For Private deployments we recommend: 1) enable envelope encryption for any tokens in transit 2) never mirror traffic from nodes with direct access to KMS plaintext (e.g., sidecars that call KMS) 3) add post-mirror scrubber if you must.
lina: How should audit logs record who enabled mirroring and which key ids were used? We need tamper-evident proof for compliance.
ops: Emit an audit event on the control plane whenever Mirror resources are created/updated. Include: initiator principal, mirror target CIDR, purpose tag, and KMS key id. Ship those events to the central audit endpoint with immutable retention.
security-bot: Suggestion: attach an HMAC-signed snapshot of the mirror config to each audit entry (sha256) and replicate to customer SIEM.
sam: Also add periodic attestation: run a job that lists all Mirror CRs and cross-checks active collector endpoints. Alert if any Collector IP is outside allowed ranges.
igor: Vulnerability triage note: if the mirror exporter has a RCE, attacker could exfiltrate mirrored flow. Ensure exporter runs in a restricted pod with PSP/psp-like policy, seccomp, and minimal capabilities.
carla: On KMS integration: don’t allow exporter to have direct decrypt rights. Use KMS proxy pattern: exporter asks control plane for ephemeral tokens (audited) and control plane performs decrypts in a hardened path.
lina: That seems like the right pattern. Any perf impact we should call out for the customer?
ops: Slight latency for proxy decrypts, but we can cache ephemeral results with strict TTL. Recommend TTL <= 1m for sensitive flows.
sam: One more: if the customer insists on mirror data leaving their VPC (to our analytics), require an encrypted tunnel (mTLS) and limit egress using VPC firewall rules.
carla: Document checklist to hand to compliance: (list) netpol E2E, audited Mirror CRs, KMS access model (proxy vs direct), exporter hardening, retention policy for mirrored data, SIEM replication, periodic attestation job.
lina: Perfect. I'll assemble a one-page runbook and link to the netpol + deploy snippet. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
